newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia rebels demand $500,000 for helicopter, crew.
newsitem.headline: Colombia rebels demand $500,000 for helicopter, crew.

text.p: Leftist rebels demanded at least $500,000 ransom for the six occupants of a civilian helicopter captured over the weekend in northwest Colombia, aviation company officials said on Monday.

A spokesman for Aeroplast, the Medellin-based company that owns and operates the captured Russian-built Mi-17 helicopter, said National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas threatened to blow up the craft if the ransom was not paid or if security forces tried to snatch it back.
Reconnaissance aircraft spotted the helicopter on Sunday, the day after it was seized, in a jungle clearing in Choco province.
The Aeroplast spokesman said rebels captured the helicopter and its occupants, including a Nicaraguan flight engineer, as they were working on installing 40 electrical pylons.
The guerrillas then forced the crew to fly the helicopter out of the area but it ran out of fuel after less than 30 miles (50 km), the spokesman said.
Police sources said the rebels may have used the helicopter to transport wounded guerrillas to receive medical treatment but the Aeroplast spokesman said he had no knowledge of that.

The ELN, a Cuban-inspired group founded by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966, shot down another Mi-17 helicopter over northeast Arauca province earlier this month, killing 20 soldiers and a civilian crew member.
